text.text_excerpt: Domilise's is a New Orleans po'boy institution. The women behind the counter are pumping out those sandwiches as fast as they can, so wait your turn in line and don't complain about the wait. Everyone else in front of you in line knows how the good the sandwich is and they are willing to wait, so you should too. The shrimp po'boy is one of, if not the best, in the city. The bread, the spicy mayo, and the size of those golden fried shrimp make it a winner. Domilise's is a little pricey for a sandwich, but they know they can be. Did you see that line out the door? Damn skippy- they can charge a little more. I've had the shrimp and the roast beef with gravy. Good stuff. I recommend this plac...

A MA ZING. If you're in NOLA for even a day and want a po-boy, you absolutely must stop here. Although I'm not a huge poboy fan, this place changed my mind. I would only ever return here for them they were that good. My friends and I shared a huge array of poboys. The spicy sausage poboy, the shrimp and roast beef poboy, the oyster poboy, and one other that I cannot recall at the moment. Out of all of these, the oyster poboy was a winner. Perfectly battered and fresh as can be. The French fries were also super good and I like that they have a bar to get your drinks at, even if it's just soda or water. BEST poboys ever! This is a small place and I heard there's normally a line out the door. My group lucked out because we were there when some of the parades were going on. You walk in, place your order at the counter with some very nice women and then wait while they make everything to order. You can see the special bread that makes this a New Orleans poboy by the door. I enjoyed the oyster/shrimp poboy (split a large with a friend). It was so good we ended up sharing another half! Everything was so fresh and, as much as I love shrimp, my surprise favorite was the fried oysters. Yummm, I'm drooling right now just thinking of it.
